handbookNote: Kentucky Real Estate Broker license exam. Part of the 2026-09-02 R26 population-tier broker buildout (states ranked 25-50 by population, after T10 and N14 were already built). Exam vendor: PSI, under contract with the Kentucky Real Estate Commission (KREC). PRIMARY-CONFIRMED by directly downloading and reading PSI's own official Kentucky Candidate Information Bulletin (Copyright 2015, updated 7/1/2015 -- the current bulletin as of this build, fetched from proctor2.psionline.com). Exam mechanics: General/National portion 80 items (150 min) + Kentucky State portion 40 items (90 min) = 120 items, 240 minutes combined, $100 fee (covers whichever portion(s) are being (re)taken). Passing: 75% correct on each portion, tracked separately (candidates who pass one portion and fail the other retake only the failed portion within 4 months). track_registry models this as exam_question_count=120, exam_duration_sec=14400, pass_percent=75, min_correct=90 (120 x 0.75 = 90 exactly). Broker eligibility: 20 hours/week for 24 months as an active sales associate, plus 21 semester credit hours (12+ in real estate) or 336 classroom hours, including a mandatory KREC-approved brokerage management course (3 semester hours / 48 classroom hours). NATIONAL PORTION -- the real PSI outline has 11 sections (confirmed via the official bulletin's own content-outline table), not the smaller ad-hoc grouping first assumed: I. Property Ownership (6 items), II. Land Use Controls and Regulations (5), III. Valuation and Market Analysis (6), IV. Financing (7), V. General Principles of Agency (11), VI. Property Condition and Disclosures (9), VII. Contracts (12), VIII. Transfer of Title (5), IX. Practice of Real Estate (12), X. Real Estate Calculations (4), XI. Specialty Areas (3) -- summing exactly to 80. Two sections (Transfer of Title, Specialty Areas) were missed in the initial 8-topic drafting pass and added as a same-day gap-fill once the real official outline was fetched and read in full. KENTUCKY STATE PORTION (40 items, per the same bulletin): Real Estate Commission general/enforcement powers (7), Requirements for a License (7), Brokerage Activities and Requirements (15, largest section -- broker/associate relationship, commissions, advertising, handling of monies/documents, place of business, records, escrow accounts, improper conduct, unlicensed assistants, broker lien law, no-call list, brokerage management), License Law Requirements for Contracts (4), Disclosures and Agency Issues (4), Property Management (3). Sourced against Kentucky Revised Statutes Chapter 324 (KRS 324) via the official Kentucky Legislature site (apps.legislature.ky.gov), read as full-text PDFs section-by-section, plus current Title 201 KAR Chapter 11 administrative regulations (via the legislature's KAR chapter index) for advertising, recordkeeping, and complaint-process rules. Two genuine drafting-assumption errors were caught and self-corrected by the drafting agents during sourcing (not left in the final bank): a supposed '$25 qualifying-broker-transfer fee' turned out to be $10 per KRS 324.287(4)(a) (a separate $200 cap applies only to broker-initiated bulk transfers of 20+ licensees), and a since-repealed regulation (201 KAR 11:062) was correctly swapped for its live replacement (11:121 Sec 9) for the transaction-recordkeeping citation. This bank was drafted across 15 parallel single-topic drafting passes (11 national + 4 initial state-law categories, expanded to 15 total after gap-fill; 5 state-law topics total: Licensing Requirements, License Status, Trust Accounts & Recovery Fund, Disciplinary Actions, Agency & Disclosures), each instructed to draft as many genuinely distinct, real, grounded questions as its topic's source material supports with NO target number or ceiling. Answers were deterministically rotated into final A/B/C/D position via scripts/tracks/rotate_broker_answers.js (global sequential-cycle rotation across all 15 bucket files combined, in file order; this generalized rotation script -- unlike earlier per-state versions -- reads the correct answer out of whatever letter it was originally drafted in, since this batch's drafting agents were told not to pre-normalize to a fixed starting letter), producing a final near-even 25.1/25.1/24.9/24.9% A/B/C/D distribution. 634 raw questions drafted against a 120-item exam -- a 5.28:1 pool ratio, clearing the standing 5:1 target.
